models_evaluated: Validated EHR machine learning algorithm predicting 6-month mortality

links.outcome: SIC rates and end-of-life outcomes versus usual care in stepped-wedge RCT
links.effect: SICs increased (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.53-2.87); end-of-life systemic therapy decreased (7.5% vs 10.4%; aOR 0.25); no effect on hospice enrollment or length of stay, inpatient death, or end-of-life ICU use.
links.quote: In adjusted analyses, the intervention was associated with increased SICs for all patients (adjusted odds ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.87]; P < .001) and decreased end-of-life systemic therapy (7.5% [72 of 957 patients] vs 10.4% [24 of 231 patients]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.11-0.57]; P = .001) relative to controls, but there was no effect on hospice enrollment or length of stay, inpatient death, or end-of-life ICU use.

links.outcome: Intervention effect on SIC rates across sociodemographic subgroups
links.effect: Effect significant across all subgroups; greater impact among Medicaid beneficiaries (5.2% vs 0.9%; aOR 2.19, P = .03 for interaction); no other significant interactions.
links.quote: The intervention effect was significant across all subgroups (eTable 2 in Supplement 2 ); interaction models revealed a greater impact on SIC rates among Medicaid beneficiaries (5.2% of encounters in the intervention group vs 0.9% in the control group; aOR, 2.19 [95% CI, 1.10-4.37]; P = .03 for interaction).

links.outcome: End-of-life systemic therapy and other end-of-life outcomes versus usual care
links.effect: End-of-life systemic therapy: 7.5% [72 of 957 patients] vs 10.4% [24 of 231 patients]; aOR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.11-0.57]; P = .001. Other end-of-life outcomes did not differ.
links.quote: Intervention patients were less likely than control patients to receive systemic therapy at the end of life (all decedents: 7.5% [72 of 957 patients] vs 10.4% [24 of 231 patients]; aOR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.11-0.57]; P = .001; high-risk decedents: 7.2% [50 of 696 patients] vs 8.3% [15 of 181 patients]; aOR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.13-1.04]; P = .06) ( Table ).

links.outcome: Serious illness conversations following risk-triggered clinician prompts specifying the intended action
links.effect: With the bundled intervention, high-risk encounter SIC rates increased from 3.4% (59 of 1754 encounters) to 13.5% (510 of 3765 encounters); aOR, 2.62 [95% CI, 1.84-3.72]; P < .001.
links.quote: Among encounters with high-risk patients, the unadjusted SIC rate was 3.4% (59 of 1754 encounters) and 13.5% (510 of 3765 encounters) in the control and intervention periods, respectively.

links.outcome: Sociodemographic differences in intervention effects on serious illness conversation rates
links.effect: Effects were significant across all subgroups and greater among Medicaid beneficiaries: 5.2% vs 0.9%; aOR, 2.19 [95% CI, 1.10-4.37]; P = .03 for interaction. No other significant interactions were found.
links.quote: The intervention effect was significant across all subgroups (eTable 2 in Supplement 2 ); interaction models revealed a greater impact on SIC rates among Medicaid beneficiaries (5.2% of encounters in the intervention group vs 0.9% in the control group; aOR, 2.19 [95% CI, 1.10-4.37]; P = .03 for interaction).
